questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: organises
Q: every year.
R: a science exhibition
S: Our school
questions.e: The subject 'Our school' comes first, then the verb 'organises', its object and the time phrase: 'Our school organises a science exhibition every year.'

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: who won the race
Q: received
R: The boy
S: a gold medal.
questions.e: 'The boy who won the race received a gold medal.' The relative clause follows the noun it describes.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: the best
Q: Honesty
R: policy.
S: is
questions.e: The well-known proverb reads 'Honesty is the best policy.'

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: The train
Q: two hours late.
R: arrived
S: at the station
questions.e: 'The train arrived at the station two hours late.' Subject, verb, place, then the extent of delay.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: on festivals.
Q: makes
R: tasty sweets
S: My mother
questions.e: 'My mother makes tasty sweets on festivals.' The subject comes first and the time phrase last.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: go to the library
Q: for their exams.
R: Many students
S: to prepare
questions.e: 'Many students go to the library to prepare for their exams.' The infinitive 'to prepare' is followed by 'for their exams'.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: After having breakfast, he picked up his bag.
Q: Ravi woke up early in the morning.
R: Finally, he left for school on his bicycle.
S: He took a bath and wore his school uniform.
questions.e: The paragraph follows the time order of the morning. It begins with waking up and ends with 'Finally', which marks the last step.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: A crow was very thirsty.
Q: It dropped pebbles into the pot one by one.
R: It found a pot with a little water at the bottom.
S: The water rose, and the crow drank it happily.
questions.e: The story runs from the problem (thirst), to the pot, the action with pebbles and the result.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Dark clouds gather in the sky.
Q: Soon heavy rain begins to fall.
R: Farmers rejoice as their fields get water.
S: The monsoon arrives in India in June.
questions.e: The events follow in natural order: arrival, clouds, rain, and the farmers' reaction. 'Soon' signals the rain comes after the clouds.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: They also process this data very quickly.
Q: They can store a huge amount of data.
R: Computers have changed the way we work.
S: That is why offices today depend heavily on them.
questions.e: The topic sentence comes first. 'They also' must follow the sentence on storing data, and 'That is why' gives the conclusion.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: received a national award.
Q: was widely praised
R: whose research on solar energy
S: The scientist
questions.e: 'The scientist whose research on solar energy was widely praised received a national award.' The clause with 'whose' sits right after the noun it describes.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: and continued till evening.
Q: Despite the heavy rain,
R: was not called off
S: the match
questions.e: 'Despite the heavy rain, the match was not called off and continued till evening.' The opening phrase leads to the subject, the verb phrase, and the added action.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: win the first prize
Q: but she also
R: broke the previous record.
S: Not only did she
questions.e: 'Not only did she win the first prize but she also broke the previous record.' 'Not only' is paired with 'but also', and 'did' needs the base form 'win'.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Therefore, we must avoid wasting it.
Q: This makes freshwater a precious resource.
R: Water covers most of the Earth's surface.
S: However, only a tiny fraction of it is fresh and fit to drink.
questions.e: The facts build up: abundant water, the contrast signalled by 'However', the consequence ('This makes') and finally the advice ('Therefore').

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Since then, it is celebrated every year as Republic Day.
Q: The Indian Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950.
R: On that day, India became a sovereign republic.
S: The date was chosen because the Purna Swaraj resolution had been declared on 26 January 1930.
questions.e: 'On that day' needs the date from the first sentence before it. The explanation of the date follows, and 'Since then' closes the paragraph.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Hence, a lack of sleep affects both memory and mood.
Q: In reality, the brain uses this time to repair itself.
R: Many people think that sleep is a waste of time.
S: It stores memories and clears away harmful waste.
questions.e: The common belief comes first, 'In reality' corrects it, 'It stores' explains how the brain repairs itself, and 'Hence' draws the conclusion.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.
P: so generous and humble.
Q: find a person
R: Rarely
S: do we
questions.e: A negative adverb at the start forces inversion: 'Rarely do we find a person so generous and humble.'

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Tea was first cultivated in China, where it was used as a medicine.
Q: Today, India is among the largest producers of tea in the world.
R: The British, who developed a liking for it, began growing it in India in the nineteenth century.
S: It later spread to Japan and, much later, to Europe through traders.
questions.e: The paragraph moves from origin in China, to spread abroad, to the British growing tea in India, and finally to the present ('Today').

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Such small connections reduce loneliness and improve their health.
Q: Thus, the real issue is not technology itself but the way we use it.
R: Yet, for the elderly living far from their families, a simple video call can be a lifeline.
S: Many believe that technology isolates people from one another.
questions.e: The common belief is stated first, 'Yet' presents the counter-example, 'Such small connections' refers back to the video call, and 'Thus' concludes.

questions.q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: The first step in solving any problem is to understand it clearly.
Q: Each of these must then be tested against the available resources.
R: Once this is done, one can list the possible solutions.
S: Only the one that passes this test deserves to be put into action.
questions.e: Understanding comes first, then listing solutions ('Once this is done'), then testing 'each of these', and finally acting on the one that passes.
